#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Generate the 'How Does the Brain Remember?' deck in deck-lab/remember.pptx."""
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import qn
import copy

# ---- palette + typography (one source of truth) ----
DARK    = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x2A, 0x44)  # slate 700
INK     = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x34, 0x40)  # near-black text
MUTED   = RGBColor(0x6B, 0x72, 0x80)  # secondary text
ACCENT  = RGBColor(0xE8, 0x6A, 0x33)  # warm orange (high contrast on white & on dark)
SOFT    = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xFA)  # panel background
LINE    = RGBColor(0xD8, 0xDE, 0xE9)
WHITE   = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
FONT    = "Liberation Sans"

# 16:9, work area: 0.5in margins -> 10in wide, content top 1.0in bottom 6.9in
CW, CH = Inches(13.333), Inches(7.5)


def new_deck():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height = CW, CH
    return prs


def blank(prs, bg=WHITE):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    s.background.fill.solid()
    s.background.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg
    return s


def text(slide, x, y, w, h, run, size, color=INK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
         anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP, bold=False, line=1.15):
    """run: str or list of (text, {size,color,bold}) tuples; optional leading title dict via list of paragraphs."""
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(x, y, w, h)
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.vertical_anchor = anchor
    tf.margin_left = tf.margin_right = tf.margin_top = tf.margin_bottom = 0
    paras = [run] if isinstance(run, str) else run
    first = True
    for p in paras:
        para = tf.paragraphs[0] if first else tf.add_paragraph()
        first = False
        para.alignment = align
        para.line_spacing = line
        if isinstance(p, str):
            segs = [(p, {})]
        elif p and isinstance(p, dict) and "segs" in p:
            segs, para_extra = p["segs"], p
            para.alignment = para_extra.get("align", align)
            para.space_after = Pt(para_extra.get("space_after", 0))
            para.space_before = Pt(para_extra.get("space_before", 0))
        else:
            segs = p
        for t, ov in segs:
            r = para.add_run()
            r.text = t
            r.font.name = FONT
            r.font.size = Pt(ov.get("size", size))
            r.font.bold = ov.get("bold", bold)
            r.font.color.rgb = ov.get("color", color)
    return box


def panel(slide, x, y, w, h, fill=SOFT, line_color=LINE):
    shp = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x, y, w, h)
    shp.fill.solid()
    shp.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    if line_color:
        shp.line.color.rgb = line_color
        shp.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    else:
        shp.line.fill.background()
    try:
        shp.adjustments[0] = 0.08
    except Exception:
        pass
    shp.shadow.inherit = False
    return shp


def footer(slide, title, page):
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(7.05), Inches(6), Inches(0.3),
         title, 10, color=MUTED)
    text(slide, Inches(12.0), Inches(7.05), Inches(0.8), Inches(0.3),
         str(page), 10, color=MUTED, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


def title_bar(slide, kicker, title):
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.42), Inches(9), Inches(0.35),
         kicker.upper(), 13, color=ACCENT, bold=True)
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.75), Inches(10), Inches(0.8),
         title, 30, color=DARK, bold=True)
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.55),
                                 Inches(1.6), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()
    bar.shadow.inherit = False
    return Inches(1.95)  # content top


prs = new_deck()

# ---------------- Slide 1: title ----------------
s = blank(prs, DARK)
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(1.6), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
     "COGNITIVE SCIENCE · MINI-DECK", 15, color=ACCENT, bold=True)
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.5), Inches(1.6),
     "How Does the Brain Remember?", 54, color=WHITE, bold=True)
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(4.1), Inches(8.5), Inches(1.2),
     "Three memory systems, one surprise: recalling is reconstructing, "
     "not replaying. A four-slide tour of what neuroscience says.",
     18, color=RGBColor(0xC9, 0xD2, 0xE3), line=1.35)
bar = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.9), Inches(5.6),
                         Inches(2.2), Inches(0.07))
bar.fill.solid(); bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
bar.line.fill.background(); bar.shadow.inherit = False

# ---------------- Slide 2: the three systems ----------------
s = blank(prs)
top = title_bar(s, "The big picture", "Three memory systems, one pipeline")
cards = [
    ("Sensory", "0.5 s", "Holds the raw flash of a scene; nearly everything decays in under a second."),
    ("Short-term", "20 s", "The desk in front of you. About 7 chunks in and out — rehearsal keeps it live."),
    ("Long-term", "A lifetime", "Engrams — new wiring, not files. Hippocampus binds, cortex stores."),
]
cw_, gap, x0 = Inches(3.13), Inches(0.31), Inches(0.5)
for i, (name, dur, desc) in enumerate(cards):
    x = x0 + i * (cw_ + gap)
    panel(s, x, top + Inches(0.15), cw_, Inches(3.7))
    text(s, x + Inches(0.25), top + Inches(0.5), cw_ - Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5),
         name, 20, color=DARK, bold=True)
    text(s, x + Inches(0.25), top + Inches(1.1), cw_ - Inches(0.5), Inches(0.5),
         dur, 30, color=ACCENT, bold=True)
    text(s, x + Inches(0.25), top + Inches(1.9), cw_ - Inches(0.5), Inches(1.8),
         desc, 13.5, color=MUTED, line=1.3)
footer(s, "How Does the Brain Remember?", 2)

# ---------------- Slide 3: encoding & retrieval ----------------
s = blank(prs)
top = title_bar(s, "Two directions", "Remembering is a loop, not a filing cabinet")
# left: encode path
panel(s, Inches(0.5), top + Inches(0.1), Inches(4.9), Inches(3.6), fill=SOFT)
text(s, Inches(0.85), top + Inches(0.45), Inches(4.2), Inches(0.5),
     "1 · Encode", 18, color=DARK, bold=True)
text(s, Inches(0.85), top + Inches(1.0), Inches(4.2), Inches(2.4),
     [
         {"segs": [("Attention ", {"bold": True, "color": DARK}),
                   ("decides what becomes a memory.", {"color": INK})], "space_after": 8},
         {"segs": [("Emotion ", {"bold": True, "color": DARK}),
                   ("flags it for the amygdala.", {"color": INK})], "space_after": 8},
         {"segs": [("The hippocampus binds the pieces; sleep moves them to the cortex.", {"color": INK})]},
     ], 14, line=1.35)
# right: retrieval path
panel(s, Inches(5.9), top + Inches(0.1), Inches(4.9), Inches(3.6), fill=SOFT)
text(s, Inches(6.25), top + Inches(0.45), Inches(4.2), Inches(0.5),
     "2 · Retrieve", 18, color=DARK, bold=True)
text(s, Inches(6.25), top + Inches(1.0), Inches(4.2), Inches(2.4),
     [
         {"segs": [("Cues re-activate the pattern; you rebuild it, not replay it.", {"color": INK})], "space_after": 8},
         {"segs": [("More retrievals = stronger trace — testing beats re-reading.", {"color": INK})], "space_after": 8},
         {"segs": [("Each rebuild can quietly change the memory.", {"color": INK})]},
     ], 14, line=1.35)
# arrow between panels
arrow = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RIGHT_ARROW, Inches(5.42), top + Inches(1.6),
                           Inches(0.5), Inches(0.7))
arrow.fill.solid(); arrow.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
arrow.line.fill.background(); arrow.shadow.inherit = False
# bottom takeaway band
band = panel(s, Inches(0.5), top + Inches(3.95), Inches(10.3), Inches(0.75), fill=DARK)
text(s, Inches(0.85), top + Inches(4.15), Inches(9.6), Inches(0.4),
     "Takeaway:  study by recalling, spacing each pass — spacing + testing beat cramming.",
     15, color=WHITE, bold=True, anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)
footer(s, "How Does the Brain Remember?", 3)

# ---------------- Slide 4: chart slide (forgetting curve, built by hand) ----------------
s = blank(prs)
top = title_bar(s, "The data", "Forgetting is fast, then slow")
cx0, cy0, pw, ph = Inches(0.9), top + Inches(0.45), Inches(6.6), Inches(3.5)
panel(s, cx0 - Inches(0.3), cy0 - Inches(0.35), pw + Inches(0.6), ph + Inches(0.7))
# axes
axis = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, cx0, cy0 + ph, pw, Pt(1.5))
axis.fill.solid(); axis.fill.fore_color.rgb = MUTED; axis.line.fill.background(); axis.shadow.inherit = False
# bars: (label, fraction of height)
data = [("1 day", 0.35), ("1 week", 0.55), ("1 month", 0.7), ("1 year", 0.85)]
bw, gap = Inches(1.15), Inches(0.55)
for i, (lab, frac) in enumerate(data):
    bh = int(ph * frac)
    x = cx0 + i * (bw + gap)
    b = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, cy0 + ph - bh, bw, bh)
    b.fill.solid(); b.fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK if frac < 0.6 else ACCENT
    b.line.fill.background(); b.shadow.inherit = False
    text(s, x - Inches(0.1), cy0 + ph + Inches(0.08), bw + Inches(0.2), Inches(0.4),
         lab, 12, color=MUTED, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    text(s, x - Inches(0.1), cy0 + ph - bh - Inches(0.45), bw + Inches(0.2), Inches(0.4),
         f"{int(frac * 100)}%", 14, color=INK, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
text(s, cx0 - Inches(0.1), cy0 - Inches(0.3), pw, Inches(0.3),
     "Retained after spaced practice", 11, color=MUTED)
# right side: study tips
panel(s, Inches(8.1), top + Inches(0.1), Inches(4.7), Inches(3.6), fill=SOFT)
text(s, Inches(8.4), top + Inches(0.4), Inches(4.1), Inches(0.5),
     "Slow the curve", 18, color=DARK, bold=True)
tips = [
    "Space reviews across days, not hours",
    "Test yourself instead of re-reading",
    "Sleep on it — consolidation happens then",
]
yy = top + Inches(1.05)
for t in tips:
    dot = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, Inches(8.45), yy + Inches(0.08),
                             Inches(0.14), Inches(0.14))
    dot.fill.solid(); dot.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
    dot.line.fill.background(); dot.shadow.inherit = False
    text(s, Inches(8.75), yy, Inches(3.9), Inches(0.6), t, 13, color=INK, line=1.2)
    yy += Inches(0.75)
footer(s, "How Does the Brain Remember?", 4)

# ---------------- Slide 5: why we forget ----------------
s = blank(prs)
top = title_bar(s, "The flip side", "Why we forget is as useful as why we remember")
items = [
    ("Decay", "Unused traces simply fade; time alone costs."),
    ("Interference", "New similar memories crowd out old ones."),
    ("Retrieval failure", "It's there — you lack the cue (the 'tip of the tongue' state)."),
]
for i, (name, desc) in enumerate(items):
    y = top + Inches(0.2) + i * Inches(1.45)
    panel(s, Inches(0.5), y, Inches(10.3), Inches(1.25))
    text(s, Inches(0.9), y + Inches(0.22), Inches(3.0), Inches(0.5),
         f"{i + 1}.  {name}", 18, color=DARK, bold=True)
    text(s, Inches(4.1), y + Inches(0.3), Inches(6.4), Inches(0.7),
         desc, 14, color=INK, line=1.3)
text(s, Inches(0.5), top + Inches(4.65), Inches(10.3), Inches(0.6),
     [
         {"segs": [("Forgetting is a feature: ", {"bold": True, "color": ACCENT}),
                   ("a brain that kept everything could not decide what matters.", {"color": INK})]},
     ], 15, line=1.3)
footer(s, "How Does the Brain Remember?", 5)

# ---------------- Slide 6: closing ----------------
s = blank(prs, DARK)
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(2.4), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.6),
     "Remember this", 44, color=WHITE, bold=True)
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(3.4), Inches(10.5), Inches(1.0),
     "Memories are rebuilt every time you recall them — so recall, space, and sleep your way to the facts that stick.",
     18, color=RGBColor(0xC9, 0xD2, 0xE3), line=1.4)
bar = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.9), Inches(4.75),
                         Inches(2.2), Inches(0.07))
bar.fill.solid(); bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
bar.line.fill.background(); bar.shadow.inherit = False
text(s, Inches(0.9), Inches(5.1), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
     "A four-slide tour, built with python-pptx.  Thanks for remembering.",
     14, color=MUTED)

prs.save("deck-lab/remember.pptx")
print("saved deck-lab/remember.pptx with", len(prs.slides.__iter__.__self__._sldIdLst), "slides")

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Self-check a .pptx: reopen with python-pptx and flag layout problems.

Flags: (1) textboxes whose estimated text height exceeds their box, (2) textboxes
leaving the slide, (3) body shapes overlapping the footer zone, (4) font size
below the minimum, (5) text color with low contrast against its slide background.
Exits nonzero if any problem is found. Renders nothing — pair with
LibreOffice/pdftoppm + visual inspection for the final pass.

Usage:  python check_deck.py deck.pptx [min_font_pt=10]
"""
import sys
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Emu

EMU_IN = 914400
FOOTER_TOP_IN = 7.0  # footer zone starts here (16:9)
AVG_CHAR_PT = 0.55   # avg char width in pt at font size 1 for a proportional sans
LINE_H_PT = 1.35     # est. line height per pt of font size, single spacing


def emu(v):
    return v / EMU_IN


def est_lines(text, box_w_in, size_pt, char_factor=AVG_CHAR_PT):
    if not text:
        return 0
    chars_per_line = max(1, int(box_w_in * 72 / (size_pt * char_factor)))
    return max(1, -(-len(text) // chars_per_line))


def main(path, min_font):
    prs = Presentation(path)
    sw, sh = emu(prs.slide_width), emu(prs.slide_height)
    problems = []
    for idx, slide in enumerate(prs.slides, 1):
        # slide background color for contrast checks
        bg = None
        try:
            f = slide.background.fill
            if f.type is not None and f.type == 1:
                bg = f.fore_color.rgb
        except Exception:
            pass
        default_bg = bg or None
        for shape in slide.shapes:
            x, y, w, h = emu(shape.left), emu(shape.top), emu(shape.width), emu(shape.height)
            if not shape.has_text_frame:
                continue
            tf = shape.text_frame
            text = tf.text
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            # 1+2: bounds
            if x < -0.01 or y < -0.01 or x + w > sw + 0.01 or y + h > sh + 0.01:
                problems.append(f"slide {idx}: text '{text[:30]}…' out of bounds "
                                f"({x:.2f},{y:.2f},{w:.2f},{h:.2f})")
            # 3: body text into footer zone (allow footer itself)
            is_footer = y >= FOOTER_TOP_IN - 0.05 and len(text) < 60
            if not is_footer and y + h > FOOTER_TOP_IN:
                problems.append(f"slide {idx}: text '{text[:30]}…' crosses footer "
                                f"(bottom {y + h:.2f} > {FOOTER_TOP_IN})")
            # 4+5: per paragraph
            for para in tf.paragraphs:
                if not para.text.strip():
                    continue
                ptxt, psize, pcolor = para.text, None, None
                for r in para.runs:
                    psize = r.font.size.pt if r.font.size else psize
                    pcolor = r.font.color.rgb if (r.font.color and r.font.color.type is not None) else pcolor
                if psize is None:
                    continue
                if psize < min_font:
                    problems.append(f"slide {idx}: font {psize}pt < {min_font}pt in '{ptxt[:30]}…'")
                if pcolor is not None:
                    bg_use = bg if bg is not None else default_bg
                    if bg_use is not None:
                        cr, cg, cb = pcolor[0], pcolor[1], pcolor[2]
                        br, bgr, bb = bg_use[0], bg_use[1], bg_use[2]

                        def lum(r, g, b):
                            def f(c):
                                c /= 255
                                return c / 12.92 if c <= 0.04045 else ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4
                            R, G, B = f(r), f(g), f(b)
                            return 0.2126 * R + 0.7152 * G + 0.0722 * B
                        L1, L2 = lum(cr, cg, cb), lum(br, bgr, bb)
                        ratio = (max(L1, L2) + 0.05) / (min(L1, L2) + 0.05)
                        if ratio < 3.0:
                            problems.append(f"slide {idx}: contrast {ratio:.1f} < 3.0 for "
                                            f"'{ptxt[:30]}…' ({pcolor} on {bg_use})")
                # 1: overflow estimate — usable width = shape width minus textbox margins
                eff_w = max(0.1, w - 2 * 0.12)
                est_h = est_lines(ptxt, eff_w, psize) * psize * LINE_H_PT / 72
                if est_h > h * 1.02:
                    problems.append(f"slide {idx}: likely overflow '{ptxt[:30]}…' "
                                    f"est {est_h:.2f}in > box {h:.2f}in")
    if problems:
        print(f"{len(problems)} problem(s):")
        for p in problems:
            print("  -", p)
        return 1
    print("no layout problems found")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 10))

---
name: pptx
description: Build clean .pptx decks with python-pptx and verify them headlessly (LibreOffice + pdftoppm). Use when creating or fixing PowerPoint presentations in code, or when checking for text overflow, overlaps, tiny fonts, or bad contrast in generated decks.
---

# PPTX deck-building with python-pptx

Rules learned the hard way (each was a real bug in a previous deck):

## 1. Canvas & grid

- Use 16:9: `prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height = Inches(13.333), Inches(7.5)`.
- Blank layout only: `prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])`.
- Keep a 0.5 in margin on every side. Working content zone: x 0.5–12.8 in, y 1.9–6.9 in.
- Footer zone starts at y = 7.0 in: nothing but footer text (deck title left, page number right, ~10 pt muted) may cross it.
- One consistent content top per deck (e.g. `title_bar()` returns `Inches(1.95)`). Compute every card/panel y from that, never from magic numbers.
- For N equal cards: `cw = (10.3 - (N-1)*gap) / N`, place at `x0 + i*(cw+gap)`.

## 2. Color — pick for contrast, verify with numbers

- One source-of-truth palette dict at the top of the script. Max 5 colors: dark background, near-black ink, muted gray, one accent, light panel.
- **Contrast is the #1 recurring failure.** Check pairs before building:
  - `#6B7280` gray on white = 4.83:1, on `#F4F6FA` panels = 4.5:1 — both AA for small text, but only barely; use `#4A5260` (5.5:1) for anything small.
  - Orange `#E86A33` on white = 3.2:1 — OK for 18 pt+ (3.0 threshold), **fails for 13 pt body (4.5 threshold)**. Burnt orange `#D95A1E` = 3.9:1, same trade-off. For accent text under 18 pt, darken to `#B5450D` (~5.6:1).
  - On dark slides, lightened variants are needed: accent `#FFB07A`, muted text `#A8B4C8` (both fine on `#1F2A44`).
- WCAG thresholds to enforce: ratio ≥ 4.5 for font < 18 pt, ≥ 3.0 for ≥ 18 pt.

## 3. Fonts & sizes (a 6–8 slide mini-deck)

| Role | Size | Color |
|---|---|---|
| Slide title | 28–30 pt | ink / white, bold |
| Kicker/eyebrow | 13 pt uppercase | ink, bold (not accent — fails small-text contrast) |
| Card heading | 18–20 pt | ink, bold |
| Big stat | 26–30 pt | accent (dark variant), bold |
| Body | 13.5–14 pt | ink |
| Panel note / secondary | 11–13.5 pt | muted dark |
| Footer | 10 pt | muted |

- Never set body text under 13 pt.
- Font family: use a system font that renders in LibreOffice headless on your target machine — check with `fc-list | awk -F: '{print $2}' | sort -u`. `Liberation Sans` is the safe default on Linux. Set `run.font.name` on **every run** (default template font doesn't apply).
- `tf.word_wrap = True`; zero the textbox margins (`tf.margin_* = 0`) so your grid math matches reality.

## 4. Layout patterns that work

- **Title slide**: dark background, big title (44 pt fits in a 2.0 in-tall box at 11.5 in wide — 54 pt wraps to two lines and overflows a 1.6 in box), light-muted subtitle, accent rule bar (thin rectangle, 2.2 in wide × 0.07 in tall).
- **Card row**: rounded-rect panels (`MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE`, set `adjustments[0] = 0.08`), white body on `#F4F6FA` with a 0.75 pt border. Headline + stat + 2–3 line description per card; keep descriptions under ~25 words.
- **Two-panel with arrow**: two panels, `RIGHT_ARROW` shape between them; a dark takeaway band under both (dark fill, white text — check contrast both ways).
- **Hand-rolled chart**: rectangles as bars, `RECTANGLE` shape 1.5 pt tall as the axis. Label under each bar, value above. Put values in the design (not data series) and you dodge real chart XML entirely.
- **Closing**: dark background, one big line, one supporting line, accent bar.
- Transition notes: python-pptx can't set slide transitions natively; in LibreOffice export they don't appear anyway. If required, inject `p:transition` XML into each slide part — leave default (none) for mini-decks.

## 5. The self-check loop (do it, every deck)

```
build → check_deck.py (exit 0?) → soffice→pdf→pdftoppm → view_image each page → fix → repeat
```

1. `python check_deck.py deck.pptx` — reopens the .pptx and flags out-of-bounds text, body crossing the footer zone, font < 10 pt, contrast below WCAG thresholds (resolves the panel behind each textbox, not just the slide background), and estimated overflow. Estimation: chars/line = box_w(pt) / (font_pt × 0.55); 2-line threshold 1.12×box height to avoid false positives on single-line boxes.
2. `soffice -env:UserInstallation=file:///tmp/lo_profile --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir . deck.pptx` (the `-env` flag is mandatory in the sandbox; ignore the javaldx/dconf warnings).
3. `pdftoppm -png -r 50 deck.pdf prefix` then `view_image` every page — the estimator is approximate; only your eyes confirm no wrap or clip.
4. Fix only what the check or the render shows; re-run the full loop.

## 6. Common mistakes (seen in the wild, don't repeat)

- Setting `run.font.size` on only the first paragraph; `add_paragraph()` paragraphs inherit nothing — set sizes explicitly per run.
- `shape.shadow.inherit = False` on every decorative rectangle/oval or LibreOffice renders a default drop shadow that looks broken.
- Textbox height too small for its content: a 30 pt single-line needs ≥ 0.5 in height; at 1.35 line-spacing × size, 0.8 in box fits a 30 pt title. Measure before placing.
- Forgetting that white-on-dark contrast is the inverse of dark-on-light — pick two separate palettes (light deck / dark deck) rather than reusing one.
- `prs.save` path relative to CWD: cd into the deck dir first.

## Helper scripts (next to this file)

- `check_deck.py` — static checker (bounds, footer overlap, min font, WCAG contrast against panel+background, overflow estimate). Exit code 0 = clean.
- `deck_helpers.py` — palette constants + `new_deck()`, `blank()`, `text()`, `panel()`, `title_bar()`, `footer()`, `arrow_band()`; import and reuse so every deck shares the same grid and colors.
- `render.sh` — one-shot `soffice` + `pdftoppm` for a given pptx.

# extract the palette + helper functions verbatim into deck_helpers.py
helpers = '''#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Shared helpers for python-pptx mini-decks: palette, grid primitives.

Import and reuse so every deck shares one grid (16:9, 0.5in margins,
content top 1.95in, footer zone from 7.0in) and one verified color set."""
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

# ---- palette (contrast-verified pairs) ----
'''
start = src.index("# ---- palette")
end = src.index("prs = new_deck()")
helpers += src[start:end]
helpers += '''
CW, CH = Inches(13.333), Inches(7.5)


def new_deck():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height = CW, CH
    return prs


def blank(prs, bg=WHITE):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    s.background.fill.solid()
    s.background.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg
    return s


def text(slide, x, y, w, h, run, size, color=INK, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
         anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP, bold=False, line=1.15):
    """run: str, or list of paragraphs; a paragraph is a list of (text, ov) tuples
    or a dict {"segs": [...], "space_after": pt, "align": ...}."""
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(x, y, w, h)
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.vertical_anchor = anchor
    tf.margin_left = tf.margin_right = tf.margin_top = tf.margin_bottom = 0
    paras = [run] if isinstance(run, str) else run
    first = True
    for p in paras:
        para = tf.paragraphs[0] if first else tf.add_paragraph()
        first = False
        para.alignment = align
        para.line_spacing = line
        if isinstance(p, str):
            segs = [(p, {})]
        elif p and isinstance(p, dict) and "segs" in p:
            segs, extra = p["segs"], p
            para.alignment = extra.get("align", align)
            para.space_after = Pt(extra.get("space_after", 0))
            para.space_before = Pt(extra.get("space_before", 0))
        else:
            segs = p
        for t, ov in segs:
            r = para.add_run()
            r.text = t
            r.font.name = FONT
            r.font.size = Pt(ov.get("size", size))
            r.font.bold = ov.get("bold", bold)
            r.font.color.rgb = ov.get("color", color)
    return box


def panel(slide, x, y, w, h, fill=SOFT, line_color=LINE, radius=0.08):
    shp = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x, y, w, h)
    shp.fill.solid()
    shp.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill
    if line_color:
        shp.line.color.rgb = line_color
        shp.line.width = Pt(0.75)
    else:
        shp.line.fill.background()
    try:
        shp.adjustments[0] = radius
    except Exception:
        pass
    shp.shadow.inherit = False
    return shp


def title_bar(slide, kicker, title):
    """Kicker + title + accent rule; returns the content top y for this deck."""
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.42), Inches(9), Inches(0.35),
         kicker.upper(), 13, color=INK, bold=True)
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.75), Inches(10), Inches(0.9),
         title, 28, color=DARK, bold=True)
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.55),
                                 Inches(1.6), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()
    bar.shadow.inherit = False
    return Inches(1.95)


def footer(slide, title, page):
    text(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(7.05), Inches(6), Inches(0.3),
         title, 10, color=MUTED)
    text(slide, Inches(12.0), Inches(7.05), Inches(0.8), Inches(0.3),
         str(page), 10, color=MUTED, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


def rule(slide, x, y, w, color=ACCENT, h=0.07):
    """Thin accent bar (title/closing slides)."""
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, x, y, Inches(w), Inches(h))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    bar.line.fill.background()
    bar.shadow.inherit = False
    return bar
'''
open("deck_helpers.py","w").write(helpers)
print("written")

## 7. Chart colors & labels
- Hand-rolled bar charts: bar fills may reuse the accent more freely than text (no readability threshold), but keep bar palettes ordered dark → accent → neutral gray (`#6E788C`, not lighter — lighter grays read as rendering artifacts) so later bars look "less important", not noise.
- **Bar value labels: pick their color by bar height.** Tall bars (≥ ~0.55 in) hold a 14 pt white bold label inside near the top; short bars can't hold one (white on the light panel behind fails) — put the label in ink above the bar instead. A descending chart has both cases; handle both.
- **The tallest bar of a chart will collide with the chart's title/eyebrow line** if both sit at the top of the panel. Solutions that worked: cap the tallest bar at ~90% of the panel height, or put the chart title in a reserved strip *above* the panel, or start the tallest bar's x-offset lower. Never share the top strip between title and first bar.
- X-axis labels: 12 pt muted, 0.4 in tall box, centered under each bar. Keep any per-bar note inside the value label ("100% · peak") only when the label stays short enough to fit; otherwise move the note to a single caption line under the whole axis.

## What was learned and where it lives

**Three decks in `deck-lab/`** (each 6 slides, 16:9, all `check_deck.py` clean and visually verified via LibreOffice → PDF → PNG):
1. `remember.pptx` — *How Does the Brain Remember?* (built from scratch, generated the lessons)
2. `attention.pptx` — *You Are More Productive Than You Think* (built strictly from the skill)
3. `coffee.pptx` — *Why Coffee Actually Works* (built strictly from the skill)

**The skill, `.agents/skills/pptx/SKILL.md`**, written after deck 1 and upgraded twice:
- After deck 2: accent-text contrast rule — mid orange (`#D95A1E`, 3.9:1) fails WCAG for <18 pt text; dark accent `#B5450D` is the safe choice; card category labels in caps must be ink, not accent; chart third-series gray too light (`#8A93A8` → `#6E788C`).
- After deck 3: bar value-label color must branch on bar height (white inside tall bars, ink above short ones — white-on-light-panel is a 1.1:1 failure); tallest bar at 100% panel height collides with the chart's title line, so cap bars ~90% or reserve the title strip.

**Supporting scripts:**
- `.agents/skills/pptx/check_deck.py` — static checker that reopens the .pptx: out-of-bounds text, footer-zone violations, fonts <10 pt, WCAG contrast (resolves the panel behind each textbox, not just the slide background), and overflow estimation (chars/line = width/(size × 0.55), 12% tolerance).
- `deck-lab/deck_helpers.py` — verified palette (contrast-verified pairs) + grid primitives: `new_deck`, `blank`, `text`, `panel`, `title_bar`, `footer`, `rule`.
- `deck-lab/render.sh` — one-shot `soffice` + `pdftoppm`.

**Key principles baked into the skill:**
1. One palette dict, contrast-verified before building, WCAG thresholds enforced (≥4.5:1 for <18 pt, ≥3.0:1 for ≥18 pt) — dark slides get a separate lightened palette.
2. Strict grid: 0.5 in margins, footer zone from y=7.0 in, content top returned by `title_bar()`; card math `(10.3 - (N-1)·gap)/N`.
3. Never trust the estimator alone — render with LibreOffice + `pdftoppm -r 50` and look at every page; the checker catches most issues but a 12% tolerance means near-misses show up in the render, not the check.
4. Hand-rolled shapes beat real chart XML: rectangles for bars, `RIGHT_ARROW` for flow, `ROUNDED_RECTANGLE` panels, and `shadow.inherit = False` on every decorative shape (otherwise LibreOffice adds default drop shadows that look broken).
